description.narrative: The project will (i) construct a new two-lane bypass road of 16.2 km skirting Batumi; and (ii) contract out routine and periodic maintenance work for about 200 km of international roads combined with connecting secondary roads based on performance-based maintenance (PBM) contract. Batumi is a major port city in the southwest part of Georgia, bordered by the Black Sea to the west and Turkey to the south. The existing main road connecting Sarpi at the border with Turkey to Poti, a major port at the Black Sea, is a key transit route along the coastline of the Black Sea for heavy goods and passenger traffic from Turkey to Tbilisi and then onto Azerbaijan and the Caspian Sea.

description.narrative: Efficiency of road transport along the EWH in Georgia improved

Travel time from Tbilisi to the border point at Lagodekhi (141 km) reduced to 1.7 hours by 2026 (baseline: 2.1 hours in 2019) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Roads Department surveys

Travel time from Sarpi to Poti reduced to 1.5 hours by 2026 (2016 baseline: 3.0 hours) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Roads Department surveys
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: New bypass road skirting Batumi constructed Indicator: New 14.3 km, two-lane bypass road skirting Batumi constructed by 2024 with an international roughness index of 3.0 m/km or less (2016 baseline: 0 km) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Civil works contract for Batumi Bypass Road was signed in Aug 2017 (JV Polatyol and Mapa).
Full access to site was provided to the Contractor in October 2018, except for 6 problematic land plots.
Unexpected ground conditions found at the project site requires additional soil investigations, which required additional time. Variations and design changes by Contractor was approved. Construction expected to be completed by end Sep 2020.
Unexploded ordnances (bombs and mines) were discovered on the site previously owned by the army which caused work interruption for several months. Site demining was completed end of Feb 2019.
During COVID-19 pandemic, site works continued. However, there were shortage in supplies due to travel/movement restrictions, which affect the overall works progress. Contractor issued a letter for force majeure.
On 28 Aug 2020, ADB approved Amendment 2 providing a 4-month interim extension of time, from 30 Aug to 31 Dec 2020 to complete the construction at no cost.
Compliance reports 1 to 6 approved by ADB.
Supplementary Agreement 2 approved on 21 May 2021 to extend the works contract until 31 Dec 2021.
Contractor encountered cash-flow situation for working capital, causing stopping of excavation works on Tunnels 1 and 2, and some bridge works.
Supplementary Agreement 3 approved on 10 Jun 2022 to extend the works contract until Dec 2022 was not signed by Contractor.
Contractor encountered cash-flow difficulty due to global increase in oil and steel prices, and shipping costs. In July 2022, Contractor stopped working but maintained token presence on the worksite. RD issued 2 notices to correct (NTC), the first in Jun 2022 and the second in Sep 2022. RD engaged with the Contractor's HO to find possible solutions to ensure that the project is provided with sufficient working capital. RD also considered termination of the Contract if the Contractor is unable to organize working capital and restart the works on critical path, but this was the least preferable option.
A joint site visit took place on 1 Nov 2022 (Employer, Contractor and Engineer) to agree on short-term milestones and respective dates for provision of materials for Tunnels 1 and 2 and resumption of works.
Engineer issued the 3rd notice to correct to Contractor at the beginning of May 2023 to take the necessary action to achieve the required IPC's measured work to ensure completion of project in a timely manner.
During Q2 2023, discussions continued between the RD and Contractor to finalize the EOT. While the Contractor has completed some works within the boundary of the Batumi Oil Terminal, it has missed all the deadlines for the relocation of the pipelines. Progress in the construction of tunnels and bridges is slow due to Contractor's lack of funds, and not enough plant/equipment and manpower is available on the site.
Minor change approved on 9 Aug 2023 to (i) remove the rehabilitation of a 21 km road section & 7 landslide sections along the Tbilisi (Gldani)-Tianeti Road from the Project's scope; and (ii) reallocate EUR9,490,000 of Category 1B.
During March 2024 review mission, Contractor indicated that based on the current progress, substantial completion of the works and opening to traffic is expected by the end June 2024.
The extended completion date of the contract was in May 2024, however, there is mutual understanding between the RD, CSC, and Contractor that a negotiated extension of time will be accorded until the date of completion/inauguration.
The Batumi Bypass Road was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of Georgia and opened to traffic on 11 Oct 2024. Currently under DNP.
To date, outstanding works are yet to be completed. Amendments to increase inputs of CSC during DNP was approved by ADB (Amendment 16).
Data Source: Supervision consultant's project progress report

Output: New Poti Bridge and approach roads, and new Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori road constructed Indicator: New 16 km, two-lane bypass road from Bakurtsikhe to Tsnori constructed by 2024, with an international roughness index of 3.0 m/km or less (2019 baseline: 0 km) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: RD sent a request in Jun 2020 to use SSS method to recruit the design consultant (Kocks Consult GmbH) to upgrade the preliminary design, technical specifications, and bidding document to a detailed design level suitable for FIDIC Pink Book for the Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road. On 29 Jul 2020, ADB approved the use of SSS method for engaging a detailed design consultant.
ADB approved the draft TOR and Cost Estimates for the supervision consultant of Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road on 27 Jul 2020. The consulting package was advertised on 30 Jul 2020.
The detailed design consultant for Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road (Kocks) signed the contract on 24 Sep 2020 and commenced the services on 25 Sep 2020.
BD for Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road Section was approved by ADB on 25 May 2021. The IFB was published on 27 May 2021. The revised bid submission deadline was on 23 July 2021. The bid opening was held on 23 Jul 2021 at RD's premises, and six (6) bids were received by the deadline.
The BER was submitted to ADB on 21 Sep 2021. ADB's no objection to contract award recommendation was sent on 22 Oct 2021.
China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) was debarred on 4 Nov 2021. Since RD issued the Notification of Award/Letter of Acceptance to CRBC on 27 Oct 2021, ADB provided clearance to RD to receive the Performance Certificate and sign the Contract Agreement.
The construction supervision consultant's contract for Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road Section was awarded to JV IRD and GMC on 19 Oct 2021. ADB received the signed contract on 2 Nov 2021.
The works contract for Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road Section with CRBC was signed on 29 Nov 2021.
Works for Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road Section commenced on 16 Mar 2022. Time for completion is 24 months.
ADB has approved Compliance Reports (CRs) 1-4 and Addendum to CR1 and CR4.
Cumulative physical progress as of end March 2024 for the Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road is approximately 69%. Concrete structures were completed, except for some remaining bridge works, and laying of pavement has commenced.
Amendment 2 to CRBC's contract approved by ADB on 28 June 2024 to extend the time for completion until 31 Aug 2024 was not signed. A new Amendment 2 extending the time for completion of contract until 31 Jul 2024 (with certain conditions) is under ADB's review.
The Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori Road was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of Georgia and opened to traffic on 31 July 2024. Currently under DNP.
ADB approved on 24 Oct 2024 the Amendment 2 to CRBC's contract to (i) extension of the time for completion of contract until 31 Jul 2024; (ii) agreements on waiver of all existing and further claims relating to extension of Time for Completion; and (iii) agreements on other related terms, including timing of Employer's taking over of the works.
Taking Over Certificate (TOC) was issued on 1 Aug 2024, and the DNP will continue until 31 Jul 2026.
Additional improvements, not part of the original contract, are ongoing and include some access roads (gravel to asphalt) to interchanges, and irrigation channels (earthen to concrete). Data Source: Supervision consultant's project progress report

Output: New Poti Bridge and approach roads, and new Bakurtsikhe-Tsnori road constructed Indicator: New 2.5 km, two-lane road crossing the Rioni River, including a 500m bridge, constructed by 2024, with an international roughness index of 3.0 m/km or less (2019 baseline: 0 km) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: RD submitted the BER on 1 Dec 2020 and ADB comments on the BER was sent on 2 Dec 2020.
ADB (Project Officer, CWTC Director, PPFD Procurement Specialist) held a meeting with RD on 22 Dec 2020 to note the following: Two bids remained which were within a reasonable distance from engineer's estimate and could be evaluated. Both companies are working currently in GEO for RD on similar projects with satisfactory performance. RD's worries over changed circumstances due to COVID-19 could be discussed and mitigated contractually. ADB noted rebidding could add 9+ months and result in less bidders with a higher price and still some risks would be unknown. RD was asked to confirm with the Deputy Minister and the confirmation email was received by ADB on 26 Dec 2020.
On 19 Jan 2021, ADB approved the BER recommending the cancellation of current tender and rebidding the contract for the construction of Poti Bridge and Access Roads.
BD for Poti Bridge and Access Roads (rebid) was approved by ADB on 21 May 2021. The IFB was published on 25 May 2021. The revised bid submission deadline was on 20 Jul 2021. The bid opening was held on 20 Jul 2021 at RD's premises, and seven (7) bids were received by the deadline.
The contract for CSC was awarded to Joint Venture ULUSLARARASI BİRLEŞMİŞ MÜŞAVİRLER MÜŞAVİRLİK HİZMETLERİ A.Ş. UBM INTERNATIONAL UNITED CONSULTANTS INC., UBM and IRD Engineering S.R.L. (the Consultant) on 11 June 2021.
The BER was submitted to ADB on 1 Sep 2021 and ADB's comments were provided on 17 Sep 2021. RD submitted the revised BER on 30 Sep 2021 and ADB's comments (2nd round) were sent on 18 Oct 2021. The revised BER was submitted to ADB on 3 Nov 2021 and currently under review.
The works contract for Poti Bridge and Access Roads (rebid) was awarded to JV Mirbud-CS on 29 Nov 2021.
Works for Poti Bridge and Access Roads commenced on 1 May 2022. Time for completion is 730 days.
ADB has approved Compliance Reports (CRs) 1 and 2.
The construction season in Poti River is limited to water temperature below 18 degrees Centigrade, i.e., between September/October and March/April.
The Contractor has completed the bridge design changes necessitated due to the upstream railway bridge and submitted it to the State Expertise Bureau for their endorsement.
As discussed during March 2024 review mission, an extension (15 months or 18 months) for completion of works is needed and the timing of such extension will be determined based on the program of works once the baseline study to establish the presence or absence of the sturgeon in the project area is completed.
Cumulative physical progress as of end April 2024 for the Poti Bridge and Access Roads is approximately 30%. Bridge re-design, necessitated due to the upstream railway bridge, was completed and is currently being reviewed for approval by the State Expertise Bureau.
On 8 Jul 2024, ADB approved Amendment No. 1 to works contract extending the time for completion until 31 Oct 2025.
Cumulative physical progress as of end Q4 2025 for the Poti Bridge and Access Roads is approximately 70%.
A review mission was fielded on 17-24 October 2025 and subsequently the extension of loan closing date to 31 December 2026 was approved to allow additional time for completing the remaining construction works for the Poti Bridge and Access Roads. Significant delays were encountered in obtaining approval for transportation of steel bridge deck components which were manufactured off-site via tunnel roads. CSC estimates that the Poti Bridge construction will continue until Q4 2026. Data Source: Supervision consultant's project progress report

Output: Detailed design, EIA, detailed LARP and bidding documents for Batumi Bypass-Sarpi road endorsed Indicator: Detailed design; and draft EIA, LARP, and bidding documents endorsed by ADB by January 2024 Achievement: N Progress/Status: The final report for Activity 1 was submitted by the consultant to RD on 25 Sep 2019. ADB received the final report on 30 Sep 2019. Activity 1 is financed under L2843-GEO
On 29 Mar 2019, a minor change in scope was approved to transfer the financing of Activity 2 (detailed design and preparation of EIA and LARP). Completion of detailed design is expected by end of 2019 or early 2020.
Due to COVID-19 pandemic, re-mobilization of the design consultants for many key tasks, such as geotechnical investigations and consultations for environment and resettlement, cannot at present be scheduled due to travel restrictions. RD confirmed during 28 Apr VC that the Board date for the ensuing loan will be most likely moved to Q3 2021 or later due to delayed completion of design.
On 16 Jul 2020, RD sent an email to inform ADB that they received the refusal letter from JV Spea and IRD on 15 Jul to continue and renew the contract due to the COVID-19 restrictions and force majeure. RD sent a letter to the consultant on 20 Jul and the consultant responded on 27 Nov. RD is closely communicating with the management of the JV members on the extension of the contract.
A VC with RD was held on 18 Jan 2021 to discuss the extension and issues concerning the Batumi Sarpi design contract. RD noted that the consultant finally agreed to extend the contract without cost implication and no additional tasks. The consultant requested to adjust the schedule and proposed replacements of some experts. The design is expected to be completed by end 2021.
RD and ADB also discussed the issue on border crossing and coastal protection, service area, traffic calculation, and tunnel design which will be communicated to the consultant once the contract is extended.
A consultation mission was fielded on 26-30 Jul and 10 Aug 2021 to discuss the design consultant's contract and the ensuing loan. It is expected that the detailed design could be completed by Q3 2022.
On 15 Aug 2022, ADB approved the extension of design consultant's contract until 24 May 2023 (Amendment 6). The design consultant remobilized on 15 Sep 2022. Detailed design activities are expected to be completed in 8 months.
Consultation mission fielded on 26-30 Sep 2022 to discuss resumption of detailed design activities. On 29 Sep, Mission met with RD and design team on site and discussed the challenges the project has to overcome.
During Mar/Apr 2023 review mission, RD indicated that further extension of the design consultant's contract is necessary due to possible changes in the design following several rounds of public consultations. Preparation of EIA would also require public consultation. Extension of contract will be processed towards the end of the contract once the situation is determined.
ADB approved on 31 May 2023 the extension of contract (Amendment 7) until 15 Jan 2024 and revised delivery dates for submission of Draft Final Design Report (30 Jun 2023) and Final Design Report (15 Dec 2023). This is due to modifications to the road alignment and considering the time required for the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture to approve the EIA document (110 days).
In Oct 2023 review mission, RD and ADB discussed the comments on the draft final report. The design consultant is currently preparing a risk analysis for the currently proposed ventilation system, which will be provided to ADB for review and input. Preparation of EIA is ongoing.
ADB approved Amendment 8 on 26 Dec 2023 extending contract completion date to 15 Jul 2024 and changing delivery date of final design report under Activity II to 15 Jun 2024.
ADB approved Amendment 9 on 9 Aug 2024 extending contract completion date to 15 Jan 2025 and changing delivery date of final design report under Activity II to 15 Dec 2024.
ADB approved Amendment 10 on 16 Jun 2025 extending contract completion date to 15 Jul 2025 as additional time is needed to review and approve the final design report. Data Source: ADB reviews and Roads Department progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N
